   • Garcia, 48 years old, was born in Peru and came to the U.S. as a young child. He became a U.S. citizen in his 20s. He is the former mayor of Long Beach, Calif., and was first elected to Congress in 2022.

   • He has said that investigating “corruption” will be one of his top priorities and has alleged that people close to the Trump family have benefited improperly from Trump’s presidency. The White House has denied this.

   • Garcia has sent a batch of letters to potential targets of investigations telling them to preserve documents. They include Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, Kimberly Guilfoyle, Corey Lewandowski, Kristi Noem and Stephen Miller, among others.

   • Garcia has said that he could go right to the federal court system if Democrats believe people who are issued subpoenas aren’t responding.    • Garcia called former President Joe Biden’s decision to pardon his family members a “mistake.” He and other lawmakers have been working for months on making changes to the power of the presidential pardon.

Five Things to Know About Robert Garcia, House Democrats’ New Top Cop
 
Plus, the Democrats set their first presidential debate for June, and Trump convenes another exclusive dinner for owners of his meme coin
 
 
JIM LO SCALZO/EPA/SHUTTERSTOCK
 

Good morning. In January, Rep. Robert Garcia (D., Calif.) will become chairman of the House Oversight Committee, an extremely powerful perch that could make him the de facto top prosecutor for Democrats (though he isn’t actually a lawyer).

 

He has already taken steps to hit the ground running, brushing aside White House warnings and putting people on notice.

 

Here are some things to know about him:

 

• Garcia, 48 years old, was born in Peru and came to the U.S. as a young child. He became a U.S. citizen in his 20s. He is the former mayor of Long Beach, Calif., and was first elected to Congress in 2022.

 

• He has said that investigating “corruption” will be one of his top priorities and has alleged that people close to the Trump family have benefited improperly from Trump’s presidency. The White House has denied this.

 

• Garcia has sent a batch of letters to potential targets of investigations telling them to preserve documents. They include Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, Kimberly Guilfoyle, Corey Lewandowski, Kristi Noem and Stephen Miller, among others.

 

• Garcia has said that he could go right to the federal court system if Democrats believe people who are issued subpoenas aren’t responding. This would remove the need to involve the Trump administration’s U.S. Attorneys for enforcement. There is a process for this, though it could take months or longer.

 

• Garcia called former President Joe Biden’s decision to pardon his family members a “mistake.” He and other lawmakers have been working for months on making changes to the power of the presidential pardon.

 

This is an edition of the Politics newsletter, bringing you an expert guide to what’s driving D.C. every day. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

People and Policies I’m Watching

 

Kim Jong Un: The North Korean leader is eager to show that he is a global statesman who doesn’t need a summit with the U.S. to prove his status.

 

Trump’s Monday: President Trump is scheduled to receive an intelligence briefing at 11 a.m. ET. Later, he is expected to deliver remarks on Protecting American Families at the Justice Department.

What I’m Following

 
 
SALWAN GEORGES/GETTY IMAGES
 

Democrats launch 2028 presidential season with new debate plans. The Democratic National Committee announced the first primary debate will be in June. It is a reminder of how soon the next presidential campaign will start to unfold. The party anticipates a wide-open and large primary field to start emerging in the months ahead. The DNC is also adding a new requirement for debate participation, saying candidates need to agree to a “fair campaign practices pledge” to join the sessions.

 

Trump rewards top owners of his declining meme coin with an exclusive dinner. The coin’s value has plummeted by around 90%, since a similar gathering in 2025. The event Sunday struggled to fill 185 seats despite it being cheaper to buy the meme coin. Trump himself made $635 million in meme-coin royalties last year, part of a $1.4 billion windfall in crypto income in 2025.

 

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed is emerging as one of his party’s most disruptive forces. The outspoken Democrat from Michigan was among the first to publicly call on Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run against New York Sen. Chuck Schumer for the party’s top leadership post. The move suggests he will shift traditional Democratic alliances in ways that unsettle both sides of the aisle.

 
 
 

What Else Is Happening

 

• U.N. climate talks collapsed after Europe and nations seeking more ambitious policies to limit global warming refused to accept a deal that didn’t call for economies to move away from burning fossil fuels.

 

• Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is the ultimate survivor in the Trump administration.

 

• The White House is planning to scale back its use of “special government employees.”
